title: The Cover of Kowloon Revisited
premise: Felix Quintana, fixer for a deniable embassy operating out of a shuttered consulate in Kowloon, answers a burner phone that rings with the voice of Marisol Vane — the colleague officially declared dead three years ago. Marisol is alive, hunted, and holding proof that the 'embassy' has been laundering atrocities for three governments, and she needs Felix to carry the truth to a tribunal that convenes in nine days. As an assassin called the Lamplighter closes in and Felix's own handlers turn predatory, Felix must choose between the only family they've ever known and the truth that will destroy it. The book ends with Felix testifying at the tribunal, the embassy burned down to its last deniable paper, and Marisol walking free while Felix accepts exile — belonging found not in an institution, but in the person they refused to betray.
about_author: Lena Blackwood is the pen name of a former foreign-service translator who spent a decade posting through East Asia before turning to fiction. She writes thrillers about people who keep secrets for a living, and she has never confirmed which parts are invented.

chapters.title: The Go-Bag Rule
chapters.summary: Felix Quintana's POV. A routine night of scrubbing an incident off the record at the Kowloon consulate introduces Felix's world: forged passports, a polished lie about who they work for, and a go-bag packed by the door. Emotional beat: competent isolation — Felix is indispensable and utterly alone.

chapters.title: A Number That Should Not Exist
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. A burner phone left in a dead drop rings with Marisol Vane's voice — the colleague the embassy buried three years ago. She gives Felix ninety seconds and a rendezvous before the line dies. Emotional beat: vertigo; the foundation of Felix's reality cracks.

chapters.title: Nine Days
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Meeting Marisol in a Chungking Mansions noodle shop, Felix learns she has documentary proof the embassy laundered a massacre in Mindanao, and a tribunal convenes in nine days. Emotional beat: dread mixed with the old warmth of loyalty rekindled.

chapters.title: The Lamplighter
chapters.summary: Assassin's POV, unnamed. The Lamplighter receives a contract: a woman and whoever she contacts. We see his methodical, almost tender professionalism as he reconstructs the noodle-shop meeting. Emotional beat: cold dread; the reader knows the clock is faster than Felix does.

chapters.title: Debrief
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Felix lies to Deputy Chief Aldous Wren about the night's movements and realizes Wren is lying back — the embassy already knows Marisol is alive. Emotional beat: paranoia; the family home has become a trap.

chapters.title: What Marisol Buried
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Flashback to Mindanao: the massacre, the orders, why she ran and let the embassy declare her dead. Emotional beat: guilt and resolve; Marisol's truth is heavy but load-bearing.

chapters.title: Three Governments, One Courier
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Mapping the obstacles — American, Chinese, and Filipino interests all want the file dead — Felix agrees to courier it to the tribunal's counsel in The Hague. Emotional beat: commitment; Felix stops being a bystander to their own life.

chapters.title: The Tail
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. A surveillance sweep across Hong Kong's ferries and escalators reveals Felix is being followed by embassy assets, not the Lamplighter — yet. Emotional beat: hunted; every familiar street turns hostile.

chapters.title: Old Debts
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Marisol calls in a favor from a retired forger who once saved her life, and he refuses — then relents at gunpoint of conscience, giving her new papers but warning that someone sold her route. Emotional beat: loyalty's price; even kindness has a ledger.

chapters.title: The Airport That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. A decoy departure through Shenzhen goes wrong; Felix escapes a detention room by burning a favor with a customs colonel, but the embassy formally brands Felix a traitor. Emotional beat: no way back; the lie Felix polished is revoked.

chapters.title: Lamplight
chapters.summary: The Lamplighter's POV. He closes on Marisol's safehouse and finds it empty — but leaves a lit lamp as a message, his signature courtesy. Emotional beat: intimate menace; the hunter is patient and almost respectful.

chapters.title: The Middleman
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Felix confronts the one handler they trusted, Ivo Reyes, and discovers Reyes has been selling routes to all three governments — the leak is inside the family. Emotional beat: betrayal sharpened by understanding; Reyes did it to survive.

chapters.title: Half a Truth
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Marisol admits to Felix that her file also implicates Felix's own signature on two of the laundered transfers. Emotional beat: rupture; loyalty and truth pull in opposite directions for the first time irreconcilably.

chapters.title: Flight Path
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. The two go dark, moving overland through Macau and onto a freighter, planning a route to Amsterdam. Emotional beat: fragile partnership rebuilt on honesty instead of institutional lies.

chapters.title: The Freighter
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Days at sea: Marisol and Felix trade confessions, and Felix decides to testify to their own complicity alongside her evidence. Emotional beat: quiet grace; belonging redefined between two people with nothing left to hide.

chapters.title: Amsterdam, Nine Hours
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Arrival and immediate ambush — the Lamplighter takes Marisol, leaving Felix alive with a message: trade the file for her. Emotional beat: devastation and clarity; the choice Felix feared is finally on the table.

chapters.title: The Exchange
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Felix offers Reyes as a false courier, trading the embassy's operational ledger to the Lamplighter's employer in exchange for Marisol — and secretly keeps the tribunal copy. Emotional beat: cunning grief; Felix saves the person by sacrificing the institution.

chapters.title: What the Lamplighter Knew
chapters.summary: The Lamplighter's POV. He verifies the trade, then discovers his employer ordered him to kill both principals anyway — and for the first time declines a contract, becoming an unpredictable third force. Emotional beat: a killer's conscience flickers.

chapters.title: The Hague
chapters.summary: Felix and Marisol POV, interleaved. Tribunal day: counsel, hostile state observers, and Wren arriving to discredit them. Emotional beat: terror of the record; truth spoken aloud for the first time.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Felix testifies — the massacre, the laundering, their own signatures — as Wren's counter-narrative collapses when Reyes's ledgers surface. The Lamplighter, watching from the gallery, lets Wren's own government take him. Emotional beat: catharsis; justice outside the law, achieved through the law anyway.

chapters.title: After the Verdict
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. The tribunal issues indictments; Marisol is free but stateless, Felix is exiled and unemployable, and the consulate is stripped bare. They part at the canal with no promises — and both keep walking in the same direction. Emotional beat: bittersweet release.

chapters.title: A Number That Does
chapters.summary: Felix's POV, epilogue. Months later in Lisbon, a burner phone rings — Marisol's voice, an ordinary dinner invitation, nothing to trade and nowhere to run. Felix answers. Emotional beat: belonging; the phone that once meant death now means home.
